component.name: Storage Wiper
component.summary: Securely wipe storage devices with DoD-compliant algorithms

description.p: Storage Wiper is a secure disk wiping tool with a modern GTK4/libadwaita interface. It provides multiple DoD-compliant algorithms for permanent data destruction on storage devices.

ul.li: 8 secure wipe algorithms including DoD 5220.22-M, Gutmann, and GOST
Support for HDDs, SSDs, NVMe, and USB drives
ATA Secure Erase for SSDs with hardware support
Real-time progress tracking with pass-level details
Automatic SSD detection with algorithm recommendations
Privilege separation via D-Bus and Polkit for security

description.p: This is a defensive security tool for proper data sanitization when decommissioning storage devices, preparing drives for resale, or ensuring data privacy.

screenshot.caption: Main window showing available disks and wipe algorithms

description.p: Health reporting fix: an NVMe module is no longer flagged for a temperature that is normal for it:

ul.li: Temperature bands follow the device class: 50/60 C for ATA and eMMC devices, 70/80 C for NVMe, whose own thermal verdict still arrives through the controller's critical warning bits
An NVMe module idling at 50 C reports good health instead of a warning
The disk tooltip shows the vendor spare threshold beside the spare capacity, so a spare warning names the value it is compared to

description.p: Preview release: accurate reporting when a helper from an older build is still running, and a restructured documentation set:

ul.li: A helper process left over from an earlier package version is reported by name, with both record types, instead of a GLib-CRITICAL and an empty device list
The Arch install hook stops an idle helper on upgrade so the next client call activates the new build, and leaves a helper that is running an operation untouched
The documentation set is organized by reader need: tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation

description.p: Reliability release: safer write recovery, stricter device and D-Bus validation:

ul.li: Wipe start rejections now name the reason: a wipe already running on the device or on an overlapping one, an unsupported or unknown algorithm, or a worker thread that could not be started
A device position that cannot be restored after bad sectors aborts the write instead of continuing at the wrong offset, and transient write errors are retried within one sector budget
Malformed WipeProgress signals are ignored instead of being parsed, and SMART data is read only for device paths that pass validation
A failed log rotation no longer silences the logger: the open file stays in use, rotation stops retrying every line, and a reopen failure falls back to the console
A second confirmation for a wipe already running is ignored instead of replacing the operation in progress
Service factories may resolve other services without deadlocking, and a circular singleton dependency reports an explicit error
Unknown command line arguments print the usage and exit 2 instead of exiting 0
The helper unit installs under the prefix's systemd directory, declares its log directory, and package upgrades no longer restart the helper mid-wipe

description.p: Feature release: firmware erase for NVMe, wipe certificates, partitions, parallel wipes:

ul.li: Hardware Secure Erase now covers NVMe drives via Sanitize (crypto erase, block erase or overwrite) with live progress, falling back to Format NVM with cryptographic erase
Every successful wipe can produce a JSON and text certificate with device identity, algorithm, NIST SP 800-88 category, timing, throughput and verification verdict
Partitions are listed next to their disks and can be wiped individually without touching the partition table or sibling partitions
Wipes on different devices run in parallel with per-device progress, cancellation and certificates
Drives with unwritable sectors are wiped as far as possible and the number of skipped sectors is reported
SSDs receive a TRIM pass after a successful wipe and its verification
The last-used algorithm and verification choice are remembered between runs
Algorithms show their NIST SP 800-88 category (Clear or Purge) in the GUI and CLI

description.p: SMART health monitoring fix and expansion release:

ul.li: Fixed the ATA SMART read that returned no data, so SATA drives no longer report health derived from an empty structure
SMART structures that carry no attributes or fail their checksum are discarded instead of reported as healthy
Added SCSI/ATA translation fallback so drives behind USB bridges and SAS controllers report SMART
Report wear level for SATA SSDs, NVMe drives and eMMC devices, plus NVMe spare capacity
Fixed temperature parsing that read vendor minimum and maximum bytes as part of the reading
Send the full SMART record over D-Bus so attributes reach the disk tooltip and the CLI JSON output
Slow SMART queries are no longer discarded; their result is used by the next disk refresh

description.p: Security hardening and bug fix release:

ul.li: Post-wipe verification implemented for Random Fill and DoD 5220.22-M via a chi-squared entropy check
Schneier, VSITR and GOST random passes now use the kernel CSPRNG
Fixed partition matching that could unmount an unrelated sibling partition
Device paths are canonicalized so symlinks cannot bypass the device whitelist
Read the ATA SMART overall-health verdict instead of assuming the drive is healthy
Show disk serial numbers when the device exposes them
Fixed a reconnect deadlock in the D-Bus client and several thread-safety issues
GetAlgorithms now requires polkit authorization like all other helper methods

description.p: Bug fix and internal cleanup release:

ul.li: Fixed missing warning and error icons in the disk row by using the actual Adwaita icon names
Migrated wipe and verification helpers to std::span buffers
Marked IWipeAlgorithm virtual methods nodiscard
Replaced ostringstream/put_time pipeline in log timestamps with std::format

description.p: New features, hardening, and reliability fixes:

ul.li: Added ATA Secure Erase support in the privileged helper
Added wipe verification with a dedicated status panel and algorithm warnings
Show SSD compatibility hint and improved disk row presentation
Require polkit authorization for device path validation
Open wipe target with O_EXCL to close mount-race window
Switched random wipe buffers to the kernel CSPRNG
Fail the wipe when fsync fails and use plain umount to preserve data consistency
Fixed sibling device unmount mismatch and disk cache invalidation before verification
Time out slow SMART queries during disk scan
Made the CLI cancel signal handler async-safe and escape JSON in CLI disk listing
Hold D-Bus proxy reference across sync calls; fall back to local algorithm metadata when the service is unreachable
Avoid locale-dependent isdigit in path matcher
Applied a clang-format pass and suppressed C2Y extension build warnings
Refactored disk API to async with callback pattern and std::expected error handling
Fixed CLI version display to use build-time version from config.h
Replaced raw GLib idle callbacks with gtkmm Glib::signal_idle()
Added RandomBufferGenerator utility for efficient random data generation
Modernized DI container: std::scoped_lock, typed enum backing, include guards
Removed redundant linter script in favor of just/meson integration

description.p: Code quality and developer tooling improvements:

ul.li: Consistent logging with structured Logger utility (ISO 8601 timestamps, log levels)
Optimized algorithm lookup from O(n) to O(1) using hash map
Refactored WipeService to eliminate code duplication
Added Clang Static Analyzer (scan-build) support
Added Valgrind memory leak detection with suppressions
Added sanitizer builds (ASAN, UBSAN, TSAN) for runtime checks
Significantly faster disk list loading with parallel SMART queries
Optimized mount table parsing (single pass instead of multiple)
Added result caching with 500ms TTL for rapid UI updates
Reduced startup time for systems with many disks
New command-line interface (storage-wiper-cli) for scripted wiping
SMART health status indicator (Good/Warning/Critical)
Post-wipe verification support for zero-fill, random-fill, and DoD algorithms
JSON output mode for CLI disk listing
Arch Linux packaging with install hooks
AppStream metainfo for software centers
Systemd service file with security hardening
Estimated time remaining (ETA) display during wipe
Desktop notifications on wipe completion
Write speed display in progress view
Expanded test coverage for all algorithms
Centralized wipe eligibility checks
Added validation for wipe algorithms
Common utility write_with_retry for reliable I/O
Updated project structure documentation
8 secure wipe algorithms
GTK4/libadwaita modern interface
D-Bus privilege separation with Polkit
Support for HDDs, SSDs, NVMe, and USB devices
